title: Overloading Operators
goal: Understand how Rust implements arithmetic operators using `std::ops` traits.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Afternoon: Standard Traits

sections.text: You overload operators in Rust by implementing traits from `std::ops`. The `+` operator corresponds to the `Add` trait.

sections.caption: Add takes ownership of self and rhs.

sections.text: The `add` method takes `self` by value. Using `+` on a non-`Copy` type moves the value into the operation.

sections.caption: Implement Add for references to avoid moving.

sections.text: To keep ownership of your values, implement `Add` for reference types like `&Point`.

explanation: Understand how Rust implements arithmetic operators using `std::ops` traits.
